items.title: 조희대 탄핵 추진 이후 첫 판사회의 열려… “재판 이유로 법관 탄핵, 헌법적 가치 훼손”

items.title: 與, 오늘 조작기소 특별검사 후보 추천
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 26일 ‘조작수사·조작기소 진상규명 특별검사’(조작기소 특검) 후보자 추천을 마무리한다. 국민의힘이 후보자 추천을 거부한 만큼 이재명 대통령은 민주당과 조국혁신당이 추천한 2명 중 1명을 특검으로 지명하게 될 것으로 전망된다. 민주당 박성준 수석대변인은 25일 최고위원회의 후 기자들과 만나 “내일(26일)까지 특검을 추천할 예정”이라며 “2, 3명 거론됐는데 그중 한 명을 추천할 것”이라고 밝혔다. 범여권 안팎에선 한동수 전 대검찰청 감찰부장, 심재철 전 서울남부지검장 등 친여권 성향으로 분류되는 법조인들이 후보군으로 거론된다. 각 당이 후보자를 추천하면 이 대통령은 3일 이내 특검을 임명해야 한다. 국민의힘 정점식 원내대표는 이날 “‘이재명 탈옥법’이라고 비판하며 장외 집회까지 하는 마당에 우리 당에서 후보자를 추천할 리 만무...

items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 25일 “바다 위의 위협 앞에서 가만히 있을 수도, 무임승차할 수도 없다”며 “국민의 생명과 안전, 국익을 지키는 일에 책임 있는 중견 강국으로서의 역할을 다하겠다”고 밝혔다. 청해부대의 작전구역을 아덴만에서 호르무즈 해협과 가까운 오만 남방 외해까지 약 2배로 넓히고 기뢰 제거 전력을 증파하는 파견 연장 동의안은 이날 국회 국방위원회 법안심사소위원회를 통과했다. 이 대통령은 이날 동의안이 소위를 통과한 후 X(옛 트위터)에 “우리 경제의 생명선인 바닷길과 선박의 안전을 확보하는 일 역시 국가의 중요 책무”라며 이같이 밝혔다. 이어 동의안에 대해 “기존 해군 구축함에 해상초계기와 소해 지원 역량을 더하고, 작전지역은 아덴만에서 오만 남방 외해까지로만 확대한다”며 “커지는 해적 위협에 대응해 우리 선원과 선박이 안심하고 항해할...

items.snippet: 정부가 대학수학능력시험(수능) 시험지 보관 기간을 현행 1년에서 5년으로 연장하기로 했다. 지난해 수능 시험지 상당수가 폐기돼 ‘인공지능(AI) 커닝’ 의혹 규명이 쉽지 않다는 비판이 나오자 뒤늦게 개선 방안을 내놓은 것이다. 교육부는 25일 자료를 내고 이런 방향으로 시험지 보관 관련 규정을 개정하겠다고 밝혔다. 교육부에 따르면, 지난해 11월 13일 치러진 2026학년도 수능 시험장 1310곳 가운데 233곳(17.8%)이 수능 시험지를 폐기한 것으로 나타났다. 현재 교육부 지침에는 시험장 학교는 1년간 시험지를 의무적으로 보관해야 하고, 이후에 자율적으로 폐기할 수 있다. 강원도는 지난해 수능 시험지를 모두 폐기했고, 인천은 시험장 학교 63곳 중 37곳(58.7%), 서울은 228곳 중 52곳(22.8%)이 시험지를 없앴다. 전북과 제...

items.title: 노란봉투법, 불복 소송이 타결의 3배… 로펌만 배 불렸다
items.snippet: 정부가 올 3월부터 노사 간 대화 촉진과 원·하청 이중 구조 완화 등을 내걸고 노란봉투법을 시행했지만, 정작 현장에서는 대화와 합의보다는 법정 다툼이 더 많은 것으로 확인됐다. 노사 합의에 이른 사업장은 14곳인 반면, 원청이 하청 노동자의 ‘진짜 사장’에 해당하는지를 판단한 노동위원회 판정에 불복해 제기된 행정소송은 45건에 달했다. 합의가 이뤄진 사업장의 세 배 넘는 수준이다. 이 때문에 “하청 노동자의 처우를 개선하겠다면서 만든 법의 최대 수혜자는 로펌”이란 말까지 나오고 있다.

items.title: Video shows massive explosion as US Army destroys entire stockpile of lead azide
items.snippet: The US Army detonates around five tonnes of degraded lead azide at an ammunition plant in Iowa, destroying the country's entire stockpile of the explosive.

items.title: “사고력 평가 아닌 탈 안나는 문제만… 수능, AI가 잘 푸는 시험 돼”
items.snippet: “대학수학능력시험은 한 문제로 인생이 갈리는 시험이 아니라, 고교 교육을 제대로 마쳤는지 확인하는 시험이어야 합니다.” 김창원(64) 경인교대 국어교육과 교수는 24일 본지 인터뷰에서 “수능도 처음에는 기본 사고력을 중심으로 평가했다. 원래 취지를 다시 돌아봐야 한다”며 이렇게 말했다. 김 교수는 2019학년도 수능 총괄 검토위원장을 맡았고, 2026학년도 수능 출제위원장을 지냈다. 2019학년도 수능에선 역대급 킬러 문항으로 꼽히는 ‘국어 31번’ 때문에 큰 비판을 받았고, 2026학년도엔 절대평가 과목인 영어가 지나치게 어렵게 출제돼 수험생들이 큰 혼란을 겪었다. 이를 모두 겪은 김 교수는 “수능이 30여 년간 운영되면서 출제진이 정답 시비를 걱정해 ‘탈이 나지 않을 문제’만 내다 보니 오히려 인공지능(AI)이 쉽게 푸는 시험이 됐다”면서...

items.title: “교사냥이 출몰 막아라”… 임용고사 시험장에 열화상·금속·전파 탐지기 투입
items.snippet: 오는 28일 전국적으로 실시되는 공립 중등 임용고사에도 ‘인공지능(AI) 커닝’ 비상이 걸렸다. 교사를 뽑는 시험 관리가 허술하다는 지적이 나오면서 시도 교육청들은 각종 대책을 내놓고 있다. 25일 교육부에 따르면, 2027학년도 공립 중등 교사 임용 1차 시험에는 6404명 모집에 4만3914명이 지원해 6.86대1의 경쟁률을 기록했다. 경쟁이 치열한 만큼 수험생들의 ‘커닝’ 불안감도 높다. 한 대학에서 교직 과정을 밟고 있는 예비 중등 교사 정모씨는 지난 18일 전국 17개 시·도 교육감을 상대로 위헌 확인 소송을 제기한 데 이어, 시험일 지정 효력정지 가처분 신청까지 냈다. 중등 교사 임용 1차 시험의 AI 부정행위 방지 대책이 부실해 기본권이 침해됐다는 이유다.

items.title: 지진은 어린이라고 봐주지 않아요
items.snippet: 25일 전남광주시 북구청 직장 어린이집에서 아이들이 지진 대피 훈련을 하고 있다. 두 손으로 안전모를 감싸 쥔 채 책상 밑에 엎드렸다. 이 어린이집은 ‘경주 지진’ 발생 10년을 맞아 이번 훈련을 실시했다고 밝혔다. 2016년 9월 발생한 경주 지진은 규모 5.8로 국내 지진 관측 사상 가장 강력했다.

items.title: 노소영측, 최태원 화해권고 거부
items.snippet: 노소영 아트센터 나비 관장이 25일 최태원 SK그룹 회장이 제안한 이혼 재산 분할 화해권고 요청을 거부했다. 최 회장 측은 지난 23일 파기환송심에서 노 관장에게 지급하라고 판결한 재산 분할금 9440억원을 모두 현금으로 지급하겠다며 대법원에 화해권고를 요청했었다. 노 관장이 최 회장의 화해 요청을 거부함에 따라 이 사건은 대법원의 재상고심 판결로 최종 확정될 전망이다. 최 회장 측은 지난 23일 재산 분할 재상고심을 맡은 대법원 2부(주심 김성수 대법관)에 ‘파기환송심에서 산정한 재산 분할액인 9440억원을 모두 내겠다’며 화해권고 결정을 요청했다. 화해권고는 재판부가 직권으로 소송 당사자에게 합의를 권고하는 절차다. 당사자들이 화해권고 결정문을 받고 2주간 이의를 제기하지 않으면 확정 판결과 같은 효력이 생긴다.

items.title: ‘가면’ 벗겨지자 세상 등진 그들… 리플리 증후군 앓았나
items.snippet: 올해 7월 치른 법학적성시험(리트·LEET) 만점자 이진우(32)씨는 지난해 대학수학능력시험에서 1문제만 틀려 서울대 치대에도 입학했다. 그런 이씨는 리트에서 만점을 받은 뒤로 수험기를 유튜브와 언론 인터뷰, 강연 등을 통해 알려왔다. 이달 들어 세무사 시험 수석 합격자가 인공지능(AI)을 이용해 부정행위를 했다는 의혹이 불거지자 이씨는 수능 문제를 실시간으로 풀어 실력을 입증하겠다고 했다. 그런데 자기 성적 알리기에 적극적이었던 이씨는 수능 당일인 지난 19일 공개 검증 자리에 나오지 않았고 서울 한 모텔에서 숨진 채 발견됐다. 이씨 죽음 후 온라인에선 ‘리플리 증후군’ 검색량이 크게 늘었다. 리플리 증후군은 거짓으로 꾸며 낸 삶을 진실처럼 믿거나 몰입하는 심리적 현상이다. 구글 검색 동향을 보여주는 ‘구글 트렌드’에서 리플리 증후군 관심도...

items.title: 한양도성 세계유산, 서대문구까지 반발
items.snippet: 국가유산청과 서울시가 한양도성 세계유산 등재를 추진 중인 것과 관련해 서울 서대문구도 “재개발 사업에 차질이 생길 수 있다”며 반발하고 나섰다. 서대문구는 홍제동 개미마을, 옛 홍제4구역 등 재개발 지역 주민 1308명 서명을 받아 유산청과 서울시에 제출했다고 25일 밝혔다. 박운기 구청장은 “세계유산 등재라는 공익적 가치를 위해 특정 지역 주민들의 일방적 희생을 요구해서는 안 된다”고 했다. 그동안 중구와 용산구가 반발해 왔는데 서대문구까지 가세한 것이다. 박 구청장은 더불어민주당 소속이다. 민주당 소속 구청장이 공식적으로 문제를 제기한 것은 이번이 처음이다.

items.title: 검사·피고인·변호인·증인… 요즘 특검 재판, 판사 빼면 다 檢 출신
items.snippet: “검찰청법 7조 1항 아시죠? 상사 지휘 거부하는 독단 행동은 검찰 조직의 책임에 반하는 것 아닙니까?”(엄희준 광주광역공소청 검사) “재판부에서 판단할 문제입니다.”(문지석 광주지방중대범죄수사청 차장)

items.title: 어린이 ‘응급실 뺑뺑이’ 뒤엔, 무너져가는 소아 중환자실 있었다
items.snippet: 지난달 28일 오전 11시 서울 종로구 서울대병원 어린이병원 소아 중환자실(PICU). 선천성 심장병을 갖고 태어난 생후 2개월 영아, 이식 수술 직후 면역력이 극도로 떨어져 격리 치료를 받는 환아 등이 생명 유지 장치를 단 채 병상에 누워 있었다. 한쪽에서는 폐 기능이 급격히 나빠진 환아에게 에크모(ECMO·체외막 산소 공급 장치)를 삽입하는 응급 시술을 앞두고 의료진이 분주하게 움직였다.

items.title: ‘진료과목 피부과’ 간판 보고 갔는데 일반의… 동네 병·의원 ‘전문의 표시 의무화’ 입법 추진
items.snippet: 경기도에 사는 김모(64)씨는 최근 피부 문제로 상담을 받기 위해 동네 의원을 찾았다. 의원 간판엔 분명 ‘진료 과목 피부과’라고 돼 있었다. 그런데 진료를 받고 돌아온 뒤, 자신을 진료한 의사가 피부과 전문의 자격이 없는 일반의라는 사실을 알게 됐다. 김씨는 “당연히 피부과 전문의인 줄 알았는데, 뭔가 속은 기분이었다”고 했다. 현행법상 피부과 전문의가 아니면 ‘○○피부과의원’이란 명칭은 쓸 수 없다. 하지만 ‘○○의원, 진료 과목 피부과’라고 표시할 순 있다. 의사 면허만 있으면 전문의 자격이 없어도 피부과 진료를 할 수 있기 때문이다. 이는 다른 진료과도 마찬가지지만, 특히 최근 젊은 의사들이 많이 진출하는 피부·미용 분야에서 전문의 자격을 둘러싼 혼란이 크다는 지적이 나온다.

items.title: [플라자] 장학재단, 같이 함께
items.snippet: 장학재단 같이함께(이사장 안대희 전 대법관)는 25일 서울 종로구 서원빌딩 사무실에서 2026년 하반기 장학금 수여식을 갖고 수용자 자녀 및 범죄 피해자, 교정 공무원 자녀 등 18명에게 4500만원을 전달했다. 같이함께는 2014년 설립돼 수용자 자녀 등이 경제적 어려움으로 학업을 포기하지 않도록 지원하는 일 등을 해오고 있다.

items.title: 30년간 우크라·몽골·말라위서 봉사, 강지헌·주수경 부부 ‘제38회 아산상’
items.snippet: 아산사회복지재단(이사장 정몽준)이 25일 우크라이나·몽골·말라위에서 30년간 의료·교육 봉사를 펼친 강지헌(66)·주수경(66) 부부에게 제38회 아산상(상금 3억원)을 시상했다. 치과의사인 강씨는 1996년 우크라이나로 건너가 의료 취약지 주민들을 진료했고, 2001년 이후에는 몽골·말라위에서 의료 봉사 등을 이어왔다. 아내 주씨는 현지 아동·여성 교육에 앞장섰다.

items.title: 정일문·김인호 ‘자랑스러운 단국인’
items.snippet: 단국대 총동창회(회장 고정용)는 ‘2026 자랑스러운 단국인’에 정일문 한국투자증권 부회장과 김인호 단국대 석학교수를 선정했다. 정 부회장은 한국투자증권 공채 출신으로 대표, 부회장까지 올랐다. 금융투자협회 비상근 부회장 등으로도 활동하고 있다. 김 교수는 2000년부터 단국대에서 동물생명공학을 연구해 왔다. 2024년 단국대 제1호 석학교수로 임명됐다. 시상식은 다음 달 3일 ‘단국대 총동창회 송년의 밤’ 행사에서 열린다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [뉴스 속의 한국사] 왕 죽인 독재자이자 전쟁 영웅… 두 얼굴 지녔어요
items.snippet: 최근 방영을 시작한 KBS 대하사극 ‘문무’는 삼국 시대 말기의 통일 전쟁을 소재로 한 드라마입니다. 그런데 주인공인 김법민(훗날의 신라 문무왕)보다 시청자들에게 더 주목받은 인물은 고구려의 연개소문(?~665)입니다. 연개소문 역을 맡은 배우가 연개소문이 정변을 일으켜 권력을 장악하는 과정을 뛰어나게 연기했기 때문이죠. 오늘은 최근 주목받는 고구려 말의 정치가이자 장군 연개소문에 대해 살펴보겠습니다.

items.title: 집 주변에 숲·산책로 많으면 더 자주 걷게 돼 사망률 낮아
items.snippet: 집 주변에 숲과 녹지가 많으면 주민들이 걷기를 더 많이 하고, 그런 환경 속에서 걷기를 많이 하는 지역일수록 사망률이 낮게 나타난다는 국내 연구 결과가 나왔다. 건강을 유지하려면 개인의 운동 노력뿐 아니라 일상적으로 몸을 움직이게 만드는 거주 환경도 중요하다는 의미다. 충북대의대 예방의학교실 엄상용 공동 연구팀은 전국 228개 행정구역을 대상으로 도시 숲의 면적 비율과 주민들의 걷기 실천율, 연령표준화 전체 사망률의 관계를 분석한 연구 결과를 국제학술지 ‘사이언티픽 리포트’ 최근 호에 발표했다.

items.title: [Dr.이은봉의 의학 연구 다이제스트] 야근할 때 ‘야식’ 먹으면 우울·불안 증가
items.snippet: 인간에 내재된 생체리듬은 밤에는 잠을 자고 낮에는 깨어서 일상생활을 하도록 한다. 하지만 회사 일 등으로 어쩔 수 없이 야근을 해야 하는 경우는 정상적인 생체리듬과 생활리듬간에 괴리가 발생한다. 지속적인 야간 근무는 기분 변화도 일으켜서, 우울증이나 불안증 발생 빈도를 25~40% 높이는 것으로 알려져 있다. 최근 하버드대 연구팀은 야간 근무 시 식사가 우울감이나 불안증에 어떤 영향을 미치는지를 조사해서 미국국립과학원회보(PNAS)에 보고했다.

items.title: 초고령화와 함께 심방세동 늘자… 펄스장 절제술 뜬다
items.snippet: 초고령사회 진입과 맞물려 최근 심방세동 환자가 급증하고 있다. 이는 비정상적인 전기 신호로 인해 심장의 위쪽 좌심방이 빠르고 불규칙하게 떨리는 부정맥을 말한다. 대한부정맥학회가 2024년 발표한 실태 연구에 따르면, 우리나라 성인의 심방세동 유병률은 2013년 1.1%에서 2022년 2.2%로 두 배로 늘었다. 이에 심방세동을 진단받은 유병 환자는 94만여 명에 이른다. 새롭게 진단받는 사람도 늘어나, 60세 이상 인구의 심방세동 유병률은 3.9%에서 5.7%로 높아졌다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [한입 테크 사전] AI 계산만 전문으로 하는 반도체… 감자 깎기에 특화된 감자칼과 같아요
items.snippet: 최근 구글이 새로운 인공지능(AI) 칩 ‘TPU 8tx’와 ‘TPU 8i 맥스’를 공개했어요. 지난 4월 내놓은 두 제품까지 더하면 올해에만 TPU(텐서 처리 장치)를 네 종류나 선보인 셈이죠. TPU는 AI를 만들고 돌리는 데 딱 맞춘 전용 칩이에요. 이렇게 AI 계산만 전문으로 하는 칩을 보통 NPU라고 불러요. ‘신경망 처리 장치(Neural Processing Unit)’의 줄임말로 AI의 바탕인 인공신경망 계산을 전문으로 처리하는 칩이에요.

items.title: 피 쏟는 산모 살려라… 자궁출혈 막는 건국대병원 어벤져스
items.snippet: 경기도 김포에 사는 33세 여성은 태아 기형으로 임신을 종결한 뒤 심각한 자궁출혈이 발생했다. 일산의 한 대학병원에서 치료받았으나 자궁출혈을 막기 위한 자궁동맥색전술을 시행하기 어려운 상황이었다. 색전술은 혈관조영술을 통해 출혈을 일으키는 자궁동맥을 막아버리는 영상의학과 중재 시술을 말한다. 결국 환자가 이송된 곳은 한강을 따라 서울 동쪽에 자리 잡은 건국대병원. 이곳 의료진이 자궁동맥색전술로 출혈을 가까스로 막아 산모를 살렸다.

items.title: ‘먼지 필터’ 코로만 숨 쉬어야 건강 지킨다

items.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
items.abstract: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies the outputs and the stored state at every decoding step. They debug against public tests under fixed budgets; their frozen designs are graded on held-out token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis, and a second track asks them to speed up a correct design at nearly fixed area. items.title: ‘어린 금수저’의 불륜 행각… 역사를 송두리째 뒤바꿨다
items.snippet: /일러스트=조선디자인랩 김가희·Midjourney KBS 대하사극이 ‘고려거란전쟁’ 이후 2년 8개월 만에 새 프로그램을 시작했다. 삼국 말의 통일 전쟁을 다룬 ‘문무’다. 이 드라마에서 지난주 3회에 죽은 인물이 김춘추의 사위 김품석(金品釋·?~642)이다. 드라마에선 초반 신라 측의 절박함을 강조하기 위해서인지 중간에 개과천선하려는 듯한 모습을 보이긴 했지만, 실제 역사 기록에선 그런 거 없이 악행과 무능과 비굴함으로 점철된 인물이었다.

items.title: ‘귀신 들려 죽여야’… 가스라이팅이 부른 참극이었나
items.snippet: 지난 10일 서울 성북구 정릉동 한 공유 숙박업소에서 15세 소녀 A양이 살해됐다. 살인 혐의로 경찰에 붙잡힌 사람은 환갑을 앞둔 남성 진모(59)씨. 숨진 소녀는 진씨 20세 아들과 사귀던 사이였다. 아들은 당시 미성년자 의제강간 혐의로 수사를 받고 있었다. 아들이 성범죄로 처벌받을 상황에 놓인 데 대한 아버지의 분노였을까. 경찰 조사에서 나온 진씨 진술은 뜻밖이었다. 진씨는 자신과 사실혼 관계였던 33세 연하 전 연인 김모(26)씨가 ‘퇴마’를 이유로 A양을 살해하라고 지시했다고 주장했다. 범행 후 A양 휴대전화를 파손해 버린 것도 김씨 지시에 따른 것이라고 했다. “A는 귀신 들렸어. 얘를 죽여야 우리 둘이 잘살 수 있어.”

items.title: 3당 합당 반대 최형우, 강원도 잠적… 노태우 굴복시켰다
items.snippet: “세계 역사를 보면 남편보다 아내가 훌륭한 사람이 결국 성공한 지도자가 되더라.” 이 말은 조병옥 박사(1894~1960)의 아내 노정면 여사가 했습니다. 가난한 정치 지망생 최형우와 약혼 후 조병옥 박사 댁으로 인사를 갔다가 이 덕담을 들은 그의 아내 원영일 (86)은 “그분이야말로 조 박사님 이상으로 훌륭한 분이었다”고 회고하더군요.

items.title: 野 “공소취소 않겠다고 못하나” 이용철 “예”
items.snippet: 이용철 법무부 장관 후보자는 24일 열린 국회 법제사법위원회 인사청문회에서 이재명 대통령 사건 공소취소 문제와 관련해 “국민이 납득하기 어려운 무리한 지휘권을 행사할 생각은 없다”고 밝혔다. 이 후보자는 그러면서도 “공소취소를 지휘하지 않겠다고는 말할 수 없냐”는 물음에는 짧게 “예”라고 답했다. 그는 “청와대로부터 공소취소 요청을 받았냐”는 물음에 “그런 적 없다”고 했다. 법조계에선 이 후보자가 ‘조작기소 특검’ 수사 결과에 따라 공소취소에 나설 가능성을 열어 뒀다는 해석이 나왔다.

items.title: ‘김병기 수사’ 1년 넘게 끌더니… 13건 의혹 중 7건만 송치

items.title: A library-based approach for inverse reconstruction of cavity depth using angle-resolved cathodoluminescence
items.abstract: In nanofabrication processes, accurate metrology is a crucial step for obtaining control over the required critical dimensions in a device. Traditionally, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is used to obtain high resolution measurements of the lateral dimension, but obtaining depth information on a thick sample is more complex. In this work, we use angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (AR-CL) spectroscopy to resolve this third dimension. Using 30 keV electrons in the SEM, CL is created at the bottom of a micrometer scale cavity milled in a gold surface. We show that reflections of the CL off the cavity sidewalls produce an interferogram which is a sensitive probe for the cavity geometry. items.title: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Color defect centers carrying electron spins in solid crystals like diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) are promising candidates for qubits and quantum sensors, with SiC material being particularly interesting due to its compatibility with the existing semiconductor technology. Here we investigated the electron spin properties of silicon vacancy centers (V1 and V2) both electron spin $S = 3/2$ in 4H-SiC in the temperature range $T=80-300$~K using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). The EPR spectrum shows central and satellite lines, where the former ones originate from V1 and V2 centers, as well as from unknown defect center X. The analysis of continuous wave EPR measurements revealed a spin concentration of $c_{\mathrm{V1}}=1.47\pm0.3\times10^{14}$, $c_{\mathrm{V2}}=5.6\pm1.12\times10^{13}$ and $c_{\mathrm{X}}=1.03\pm0.21\times10^{13}$ spins/cm$^{3}$. items.title: Design, Testing and Calibration of the GAPS Experiment Si(Li) Tracker Readout ASIC: From the First Flight Campaign Toward the Second Mission Upgrade
items.abstract: The General Antiparticle Spectrometer (GAPS) is a balloon-borne experiment designed to perform three long-duration flights from Antarctica to search for low-energy cosmic antinuclei, in particular antideuterons, as an indirect signature of dark matter. Its detection method relies on the formation and decay of exotic atoms, identified through the emission of characteristic x-rays and the subsequent annihilation into secondary particles. At the core of the instrument is the silicon tracker, composed of lithium-drifted silicon detectors operated at -40°C and read out by a custom application-specific integrated circuit, SLIDER32, implemented in 180 nm CMOS technology. This thesis reports on the integration, calibration, and validation of the SLIDER32-based tracker readout electronics. Laboratory characterization of a tracker module with an Am-241 source and cosmic muons was complemented by c...

Certified minimax normal-scale mixtures for the logistic-normal integral
items.abstract: The logistic distribution function is a scale mixture of normal distribution functions, and Monahan and Stefanski approximate it by the $K$-term mixture $Λ(x) \approx \sum_{i} w_i Φ(s_i x)$ chosen to minimise the uniform error on the real line. Each such mixture reduces the logistic-normal integral to a sum of $K$ normal distribution functions with the mixture's uniform error bound. This integral is the expectation of a logistic sigmoid over a normal distribution in statistics and the Gauss-Fermi integral in semiconductor physics. Monahan and Stefanski tabulate constants for $K \le 8$ and conjecture that the optimal error equioscillates at $2K$ points, while above $K = 8$ the Remez exchange and local solvers stall at nonequioscillating stationary points. We prove that the tangent space of the mixture family is a Chebyshev system, which forces $2K$-point equioscillation at every interior...

items.title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
items.abstract: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). items.title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
items.abstract: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface. We experimentally demonstrate the first N-polar AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on GaN substrate without emitter regrowth. The HBTs exhibit a peak current gain of approximately 15, peak differential current gain of approximately 18, and emitter-area-normalized peak current densities exceeding 20 kA/cm^2 and 66 kA/cm^2 for emitter areas of 10 x 10 um^2 and 3 x 10 um^2, respectively. items.title: Real-Time AI Acceleration on a 2D Spatial Dataflow Architecture
items.abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is increasingly being integrated into real-time systems, which makes the timing analysis of ML accelerators necessary. However, the most popular commercial accelerator, the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU), remains difficult to analyze as several aspects of its behavior, including scheduling of threads involved in single-instruction multiple-thread computations and memory access latency, are not fully documented. Spatial dataflow accelerators present an interesting alternative to GPUs, as they inherently support compute and memory partitioning. Data movement and computation locality are explicitly controlled by the programmer. In this work, we consider the Tenstorrent Blackhole, which is based on a commodity RISC-V architecture. items.title: Neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional phonon Boltzmann-Fourier coupling for multiscale heat transport in silicon fin arrays
items.abstract: Localized heating in semiconductor devices can produce non-diffusive phonon transport near heat-generating regions, while heat spreading through the surrounding substrate remains well described by Fourier conduction. We present a hybrid framework that couples a pretrained neural operator for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) within individual fins to a Fourier model of a shared substrate. To reduce the cost of repeated BTE solves across fin positions and coupling iterations, a DeepONet maps each fin's substrate-interface temperature and heating state to its temperature and heat-flux fields. The operator is trained on interface temperatures generated by a linearized proxy of the coupled problem, which avoids explicit training data collection from full coupled runs. items.title: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
items.abstract: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. We trace this hierarchy to the redistribution of noise-sensitive channels away from zero frequency and show it to hold for noise spectra dominated by low-frequency weight, including $1/f$ and Lorentzian. items.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
items.abstract: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. items.title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. items.title: Anatomy of orbital and spin responses in GaAs and Si: Hall, inverse Faraday, and magneto-optical Kerr effects
items.abstract: Magneto-optical signals in nonmagnetic semiconductors entangle spin and orbital contributions, both in angular-momentum generation and magneto-optical detection. We calculate these contributions for electron-doped GaAs and Si using density-functional theory, linear-response theory, and a second-order density-matrix treatment of the inverse Faraday effect. items.title: Numerical simulations of CCP-2D GEC with sGMRES
items.abstract: Fluid models provide an efficient means of simulating the low-temperature gas discharges, which are important in semiconductor manufacturing. This work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first systematic numerical framework for the Gaseous Electronics Conference (GEC) reference cell of the 2D capacitively coupled plasma (CCP). The framework employs a structured, nonuniform cylindrical mesh to resolve the spatial gradients. A semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is used for the Poisson's equation, while the implicit SG schemes are applied to the continuity equations and the electron energy equation. Both the explicit and and the implicit formulations based on the conventional drift-diffusion terms are also investigated. items.title: Indentation-induced polar domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave semiconductor EuTe4
items.abstract: Controlling polar domains in conducting materials by external fields could unlock polarization-based electronic functionalities, yet remains experimentally challenging. While mechanical actuation driven by local strain, stress, or strain gradients has been proposed as an external-voltage-free route, its experimental demonstration in relatively conducting polar materials remains limited. Here we demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave (CDW) semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, whose resistivity is on the order of 10 m$Ω$cm. Polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements reveal CDW-induced in-plane polarization domains with an approximately 90 $^\circ$ domain configuration. items.title: Proposal for a cat-cluster-state machine gun
items.abstract: Non-Gaussian bosonic states such as the Schrödinger cat states are essential for continuous-variable quantum-information processing. A convenient and deterministic process for generating cat states is through the use of a Rabi interaction between a single bosonic mode and a spin which facilitates a state-dependent displacement. The lack of a Rabi interaction for propagating optical photons has rendered optical cat states elusive. Here, we show that the complex nonlinear scattering dynamics of a single-mode squeezed-vacuum state interacting with a quantum emitter can be engineered to produce a Rabi interaction between a quantum emitter and a propagating photon mode while the contributions from other orthogonal modes destructively interfere. items.title: Population of spin orbit-split-electron branches in semimetallic HgTe quantum wells
items.abstract: We present the results of experimental studies on magnetoresistance, the Hall effect, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations performed in gated heterostructures with HgTe-based gapless semiconductor quantum wells. We show that in quantum wells with widths corresponding to a semimetallic charge carrier spectrum, electrons, in contrast to the idealized model, populate both spin-orbit-split branches of the spectrum. This occurs regardless of whether the Fermi level lies exclusively in the conduction band or within the conduction-valence band overlap region.

items.title: AgenticMM: A Material-Centered Multi-Agent Architecture for Scalable First-Principles Materials Modeling
items.abstract: Multi-agent frameworks are attracting increasing attention as a means of autonomously driving complex, long-running workflows in first-principles materials modeling. However, such frameworks commonly organize AI agents by computational task or scientific role. When scaled across many materials, this organization can require repeated transfers of material-specific context and complicate persistent execution and resource coordination. Here, we introduce AgenticMM, a material-centered multi-agent architecture in which each material has a persistent agent that owns its complete workflow and retains its scientific context, while a persistent coordinator allocates shared resources, mediates communication, and tracks campaign progress. items.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
items.abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. items.title: First-Principles Investigation of the {ScSe2} TMDs Monolayer: Structural Stability, Electronic and Optical Properties
items.abstract: We present an ab initio investigation of the {ScSe2} monolayer using density functional theory (DFT), as employed in the CP2K code, to assess its structural stability and electronic properties. The electronic behavior of both phases is governed by the local coordination environment of scandium and the associated lifting of degeneracy of its $3d$ orbitals. The valence bands (VBs) are dominated by {Se}$-4p$ states in both phases, while the states near the Fermi level distinguish the metallic 1T phase from the semiconducting 2H phase. Optical response calculations reveal markedly different spectral signatures for the two polymorphs. Two findings emerge from this study: a polymorphism-driven metal-to-semiconductor transition without any change in chemical composition and distinct optical responses relevant to phase-selective optoelectronic devices.

items.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
items.abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.

items.title: Metal to Semiconductor Transition in Niobium Sulfoselenide Alloy Films by Compositional Control
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have garnered significant interest due to their tunable bandgaps, optical anisotropy, and mechanical flexibility. This study explores the relationship between stoichiometry, structural phase, and electronic transport in niobium sulfoselenide (NbSxSe2-x) thin films. In this study, low-dimensional TMD films were grown with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) to investigate the effects of varying chalcogen (sulfur and selenium) content in NbSxSe2-x alloys. We focus on tuning electrical resistivity along with the transition from metallic-to-semiconducting behavior through compositional control. These MBE grown films were characterized using in-vacuo x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to analyze the chemical composition. items.title: Optical Scintillation Imaging for Dynamic Source Tracking Dosimetry During Prostate HDR Brachytherapy
items.abstract: High-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy is highly conformal, but its accuracy depends on catheter and source placement, and clinical workflows lack real-time in vivo dosimetry (IVD) that verifies delivery without disrupting the procedure. We characterize a scintillator-based optical dosimeter integrated into a transrectal probe that tracks source position, speed, dose rate, and time-resolved cumulative dose. A 67 mm x 5 mm line scintillator is imaged by a CMOS camera through a 30-degree endoscopic lens; geometric and flat-field corrections remove barrel distortion and vignetting. Absolute dose was calibrated with a TOPAS Monte Carlo model of the probe's air-cavity geometry. The system was validated in a water phantom with an Ir-192 source and needles at radial offsets of 7, 10, and 15 mm. Response varied by $\pm$2\% along the 67 mm scintillator and was linear over 5-21 cGy/s ($R^2 \geq 0.995$...

items.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. The system also navigates the charge-stability landscape to stabilize the quantum dot around optimal operati...

items.title: Coherence Lengths of Laser Pointers
items.abstract: We report on the coherence lengths of low-cost green laser pointers in the midst of multimodal behavior using an optical interferometer based on noncollinear beam geometries and a CMOS detector array. Examined devices include three diode lasers and a frequency-doubled neodymium-emission diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) laser. Coherence length measurements are variable among devices, but values can nevertheless regularly exceed 10 cm. The work serves as a template for an advanced undergraduate physics laboratory experiment and may inspire new kinds of laser pointer devices utilizing interference effects as operative principles.

items.title: Specification-Grounded Adaptive Triage and Formal Invariant Exclusion Synthesis for Autonomous Silicon Coverage Closure
items.abstract: Closing the final 5%-15% of code and functional coverage remains a major schedule bottleneck in silicon tapeouts. Existing LLM-based coverage closure loops feed raw uncovered RTL lines or branches directly into iterative prompts, failing on industrial subsystems due to: (1) token and context explosion from querying thousands of correlated holes independently; (2) illegal stimulus that violates cross-signal invariants and yields dirty coverage; and (3) unsafe exclusion hallucination on structurally unreachable dead code. We present ARGUS (Autonomous Reachability & Guided Unified Stimulus), a specification-grounded, dual-regime coverage closure and formal exclusion synthesis engine. items.abstract: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. items.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
items.abstract: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. items.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
items.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). items.title: CRAFT: Analog Circuit Design by Reasoning LLM Agents from Pre-Computed Lookup Tables
items.abstract: Automated analog circuit sizing methods, from black-box optimizers to recent large language model (LLM) agents, typically search the design space with a SPICE simulator in the loop, whereas an experienced designer works out a design by hand analysis. This paper presents CRAFT, a flow in which an LLM agent designs a given topology by calculation, as a designer does, and without an initial sizing. The agent works only through DeX, a service that uses pre-computed lookup tables to provide device characteristics and to solve the whole netlist for its operating point and small-signal response. It thus designs without SPICE, and every final design is verified independently in HSPICE. We test CRAFT on four circuits in a commercial 28 nm process; the largest is a 37-transistor three-stage amplifier with 53 design variables, 20 specifications and 74 saturation constraints. items.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
items.abstract: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{MAX} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{BR}I_{MAX}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.

items.title: Optical readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors with SiPMs
items.abstract: Scintillation light readout of MicroPattern Gaseous Detectors (MPGDs) is used for imaging and track reconstruction applications including in optical Time Projection Chambers (TPC). Typically, high resolution CCD or CMOS imaging sensors are used and PMTs can be employed to obtain auxiliary timing information. We report on the optical readout of MPGDs with Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) which enables limited spatial resolution. Arrays of SiPMs were used to read out Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Glass Micromegas amplification stages. Center of gravity reconstruction of hit positions yields a spatial resolution of approximately 1.35 mm for signals shared across multiple SiPMs. High gain of the amplification stage as well as the SiPMs enables good signal sharing and is advantageous for position reconstruction.

items.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
items.abstract: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis. Consequently, sub-digital processors could potentially offer a viable, near-term solution to drastically reduce the energy demands of AI.

items.title: Delay Mismatches Shape the Spectra of Three Synchronized Semiconductor Lasers
items.abstract: We study a network of three synchronized chaotic lasers and the radio frequency spectra of the intensity fluctuations. The position and morphology of the peaks are significantly different depending on the set of lasers being synchronized. The lasers and coupling paths are similar but not identical in all parameters, including their feedback and coupling delay times. The inverse of the delay mismatch between each pair of lasers introduces characteristic frequencies that shape the spectral response of the synchronized system. By studying two different three-laser configurations, we find that peaks appear whenever multiple harmonic contributions overlap in frequency, resulting in constructive enhancement of the spectral power. items.title: Ultrafast Successive Control and Electrical Detection of Long-Lived Valley Polarization in Room-Temperature Germanium
items.abstract: Germanium (Ge) hosts four degenerate valleys in the conduction band minima, and their highly anisotropic effective masses offer a valley degree of freedom in transport phenomena via anisotropic conductivity. Using time- and polarization-resolved terahertz spectroscopy combined with deformation potential theory, we reveal a valley relaxation time reaching 10 ps near the band edge of Ge(001) at room temperature, long enough to detect the valley polarization in electrical transport measurements. We also demonstrate sub-picosecond complete reversal of valley polarization by off-resonant light pulses at extremely low energy consumption. These results pave the way for room-temperature valleytronics based on bulk indirect-gap semiconductors compatible with existing electronics.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
items.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. Our quantum processor receives an input...

Tuning spreading transport in GaN HEMTs with an AlN space layer under non-equilibrium heating
items.abstract: Lateral spreading transport dominates near-junction heat dissipation in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, yet thermal control has largely overlooked this geometry. It neither reaches the core AlGaN/GaN region nor, beyond the spatial spreading itself, accounts for the spectral non-equilibrium of the heat source. Here we tune the spreading resistance directly by inserting a thin, highly conducting AlN space layer above the source to intercept heat and divert it laterally. We test this approach across GaN, AlGaN/GaN, and AlGaN/AlN/GaN structures under both equilibrium and longitudinal-optical (LO)-pumped non-equilibrium heating, pairing non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) with full-band phonon Monte Carlo (MC). In equilibrium, the AlN layer lowers the spreading resistance by 38% relative to the AlGaN-capped structure and by 17% relative to bare GaN, with little change in the one...

items.title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
items.abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. items.title: A Probabilistic Behavioral RTL Simulation Framework for Probabilistic Compute Fabrics
items.abstract: Coupled oscillator Ising hardware can produce different solution qualities across repeated runs of the same problem, while a deterministic behavioral model used for the design yields a single outcome under fixed conditions. Capturing this stochastic variability during design time is essential for evaluating how closely simulation reflects silicon behavior. This work presents a probabilistic behavioral RTL simulation framework that introduces Gaussian timing variation into coupling delays. This variation changes oscillator timing during evolution, producing different outcomes across runs while retaining the existing chip control and readout blocks. The framework is evaluated against measurements from two chips: a 28-nm CMOS chip with 66 spins and a 16-nm FinFET chip with 49 spins, using 250 problems run 100 times repetitively. Compared with deterministic simulation, the model reduces the...

items.title: ADSPICE: A Method of Automatic Differentiation for Gradient-Based Lumped Circuit Optimization with Native SPICE
items.abstract: This work presents a novel computer-aided design (CAD) tool for gradient-based circuit optimization using SPICE and automatic differentiation, which we term ADSPICE. Automatic differentiation (AD) is a technique for evaluating a derivative by breaking it into its elementary differentiation operations and repeatedly applying the chain rule, in contrast with a finite-difference-based derivative computed from a small perturbation. Native SPICE (realized with ngspice) is equipped with automatic differentiation toward gradient-based optimization, particularly adjoint-mode optimization. This is implemented with custom C code and shared library control, allowing easy integration with existing SPICE infrastructure. We show a computational performance analysis, demonstrating faster optimization vs. an existing finite-difference method, SPICE OPUS, the closest competitor in SPICE optimization tool...

items.title: Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
items.abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. While quantum phase fluctuations suppress the $6e$ coherence, we show that through spin-or...

items.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
items.abstract: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication. Here, we overcome this challenge by integrating multiple NV centers into a monolithic diamond photonic crystal nanocavity while preserving near-lifetime-limited optical coherence. We observe linewidths as narrow as 19 MHz, enabling the frequency multiplexing of spectrally distinct NV centers within a common cavity mode, while maintaining charge-state stability over several minutes under resonant excitation. Tuning the cavity into resonance with the NV zero-phonon line enhances the optical emission, consistent with Purcell enhancement predicted by finite-element simulations. In this work, we study routing in these recently proposed inter-chiplet interconnect topologies by categorizing and evaluating nine deadlock-free routing functions for irregular topologies known from data center networking in this new context. items.title: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems
items.abstract: Accurate magnetic-field evolution of spectra requires a common wavefunction representation that consistently describes multiple states across different field regimes. Discrete Variable Representation (DVR) methods combine accurate basis-based kinetic-energy evaluation with flexible real-space potential representation, enabling arbitrary non-analytic potentials to be treated. Here, we develop a magnetic-field-dependent Hermite function-based (Hermite-B) DVR that adapts naturally to magnetic confinement, efficiently representing compressed wavefunctions across a wide range of field strengths while remaining centered in regions relevant to the scalar confinement potential. This ensures accurate treatment of the field-dependent kinetic energy while addressing two key challenges: maintaining accuracy from the Zeeman to Landau regimes and accommodating diverse confinement potentials. items.title: How well does graph superoptimization transfer? Adapting tensor-graph superoptimizer to a Triton-based NPU

We investigate how well graph-level superoptimization transfers across architectures by adapting Mirage from its CUDA-oriented design to the Huawei Ascend 910B3 through a Triton-based compilation stack. The results show that graph-level optimization can successfully transfer and outperform available reference implementations by up to 87.0% on fused workloads. However, performance is highly dependent on tensor shape and workload structure, with substantial regressions for other configurations. items.abstract: We combine first-principles calculations with structural, magnetic, and transport measurements to investigate the influence of chemical disorder on the quaternary Heusler alloy NiMnCrAl. items.title: Performance limits and benchmarking of ideal 2D topological insulator field-effect transistors
items.abstract: Topological insulator field-effect transistors (TIFETs) have emerged as a promising alternative to overcome the scaling limits of silicon-based field-effect transistors (Si-based FETs). In this study, we establish the performance limits of ideal TIFETs and present a comprehensive benchmarking of the switching energy-delay performance of TIFETs against Si-based FETs (FinFET and LGAA) and 2-D material-based FETs ($\mathrm{MoS}_2$ and InSe) under equivalent and realistic conditions. Furthermore, we analyze the key factors influencing the switching energy-delay performance of TIFETs, including contact resistance ($R_{\mathrm{C}}$), parasitic capacitance ($C_{\mathrm{par}}$), channel length ($L$), and channel width ($W$). Notably, TIFETs achieve substantially lower switching energy and delay time, outperforming both Si-based FETs and 2-D material-based FETs, where a transition from 1-stack to...

items.title: Sub-electron noise with a buried-channel DePFET: characterisation of novel DePFET concepts
items.abstract: Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DePFET) pixel sensors combine Fano-limited energy resolution with fast, low-noise readout and are used in instruments ranging from particle tracking to X-ray astronomy. In this work, two novel DePFET technologies that address the two factors of the signal-to-noise ratio through fundamental changes to the intrinsic design are characterised: a buried-channel design aimed at reducing the limiting low-frequency noise by weakening the coupling between the channel and Si/SiO$_2$ interface traps, and a super-$g_q$ design intended to increase the charge gain by reducing the effective internal-gate capacitance. items.title: Generating Circularly Polarized and Chiral Cathodoluminescence from a Single Plasmonic Nanoantenna
items.abstract: The generation and control of circularly polarized and chiral light is important for a wide range of applications, from sensing to optical communication and catalysis. Generally, the generation of chiral light emission from plasmonic nanostructures relies on the use of nanoantennas with predefined chiral shape, which requires complex nanofabrication. In this work, we show how localized electron excitation controls the generation of circularly polarized- and chiral cathodoluminescence from a single achiral plasmonic nanoantenna. We exploit the $π$/2 phase difference between the transverse and longitudinal components of the electric field that is carried by 30 keV electrons, to coherently excite degenerate dipolar modes of which the far-field radiation interferes in the far field, thereby creating a strong optical spin-Hall effect. items.title: Koopmans spectral functionals for excitons in materials
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles characterization of excitons typically relies on the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) combined with quasiparticle energies from computationally demanding GW calculations. Here, we replace the GW step with quasiparticle energies from Koopmans-compliant spectral functionals, an approach we call BSE@qKI, and implement it in an automated, reproducible AiiDA workflow. For a set of benchmark semiconductors, BSE@qKI reproduces experimental band gaps and first exciton energies with mean absolute relative errors of 13% and 4%, respectively, comparable to BSE@G0W0 for the gaps and markedly better for the excitation energies. We also apply the method to the layered magnetic semiconductor CrI3, obtaining an absorption spectrum that reproduces the main experimental features. These results establish BSE@qKI as a GW-free alternative to BSE@G0W0 for systematic studies of excitonic...

items.title: A Discrete Digital Isolator with Shielded Planar Transformer for Gate Driver Applications
items.abstract: Galvanically isolated gate drivers are required in many power electronics applications. This paper describes an implementation of a digital isolator using discrete components with a planar coreless PCB signal transformer providing the isolation. The use of an electrostatic shield between the transformer windings is shown to provide sufficient common-mode transient immunity to support IGBT half-bridge drivers, an application subject to a severe dV/dt transient during switching. The design is verified through the experimental implementation of a prototype half bridge using two of the proposed discrete digital isolators with SiC power transistors and demonstrates common-mode transient immunity greater than 15 kV/us with very low implementation complexity.

items.abstract: We assess the performance of electric-field-induced forces for bulk solids within the projector-augmented wave method. items.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
items.abstract: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. items.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
items.abstract: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light. items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field inse...

items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. items.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-tran...

items.title: BROAD: Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM
items.abstract: Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present BROAD, or Bit-Parallel Row-Oriented Arithmetic in DRAM. BROAD augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. These pri...

items.title: SPLASH: Co-Designing Flash-Aware Sparse Attention with a Virtualized HBM-HBF Hierarchy
items.abstract: As context lengths, request lifetimes and concurrency grow, the key-value (KV) cache dominates memory usage in large language model (LLM) inference. High-bandwidth memory (HBM), the memory on contemporary GPUs, achieves far higher bandwidth than off-package memory, yet its capacity, bounded by DRAM density, has not kept pace with this demand. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF), an emerging memory technology, bridges this gap, combining the advanced packaging of HBM with the density of flash to deliver terabyte-scale capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth. Exploiting this capacity for long-context KV caches, however, requires hiding the vastly different physical characteristics of flash from the GPU while keeping decode interactive. We therefore introduce Splash, an architecture that virtualizes HBM and HBF for the KV cache. We architect custom HBM and HBF base dies with novel memory and flash cont...

items.title: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
items.abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures enable the combination of two-dimensional (2D) materials with different electronic properties in a single device. Bilayer graphene (BLG) is particularly attractive as its electrically tunable band gap enables local control of tunnel barriers and quantum dots (QDs). Here, we realize an all-2D hybrid platform based on BLG proximitized by superconducting NbSe$_2$. Using electrostatic gates, we define tunnel barriers and QDs at different distances from the superconductor-semiconductor interface. The QDs serve as local spectroscopic probes of the proximitized BLG channel, forming tunable superconductor-quantum dot-normal conductor junctions. Coulomb blockade and finite-bias spectroscopy reveal a proximity-induced superconducting gap of up to $80\,\mathrm{μeV}$ and allow to track its evolution with distance from the NbSe$_2$ contact. The local density of states r...

items.title: Continuous-Wave Operation at 30 MV/m of a Superconducting Radio-Frequency Gun Cryomodule with an Exchangeable Cathode Plug
items.abstract: A prototype 185.7 MHz superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) electron gun cryomodule has been developed for the proposed LCLS-II-HE Low Emittance Injector at SLAC. It has an in-situ ultra-high-vacuum exchangeable cathode plug system compatible with semiconductor photocathodes. With a copper plug, the gun achieved continuous-wave RF operation at a cathode field of 30 MV/m. No measurable degradation was observed after plug removal and reinsertion with the cavity at 4.4 K. This result is a significant improvement over past continuous-wave SRF gun systems with exchangeable plugs.

items.title: Heteroepitaxial Growth of PbSe on InP via III-V Buffer Layers
items.abstract: Detector cost remains a barrier to the widespread adoption of mid-wave infrared (3-5 micron) technology. PbSe, an inexpensive narrow band gap IV-VI semiconductor that has been used since the early 1940s, delivers high performance for infrared detection despite the abundance of grain boundaries in polycrystalline films. Epitaxial growth, however, could provide superior crystalline quality and interfaces, but suitable substrates remain limited for PbSe. Recent PbSe heteroepitaxy has focused primarily on III-V, II-VI and group-IV substrates that each offer a comparatively narrow range of lattice-matched alloys for heterostructure engineering. Here we show that InP-based heteroepitaxy provides access to a broader materials platform while limiting the lattice mismatch with PbSe to approximately 4%. We grow 151-nm thick PbSe films by molecular beam epitaxy on 200-nm thick In0.53Ga0.47As and In...

items.title: Thermoelectric properties of metal-semiconductor percolation composites
items.abstract: We analyze the thermoelectric response of composite materials comprising homogeneous semiconductor hosts with randomly distributed metallic inclusions. We demonstrate that the properties of such materials are strongly affected by the percolation transition (with background conductivity). We show that in the vicinity of the percolation threshold, the power factor and the thermoelectric figure of merit strongly depend on both the concentration and arrangement of inclusions. Finally, we identify promising regimes for enhancing the power factor in realistic composites.

items.title: Josephson effect in bipolar magnetic semiconductors
items.abstract: We theoretically investigate equilibrium currents in a one-dimensional Josephson junction incorporating a bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS). We show that the intrinsic exchange splitting of the spin-resolved bands enables purely electrical control of the $0$--$π$ transition through gate-tunable modulation of the BMS chemical potential, eliminating the need for an external magnetic field. This provides a viable route toward electrically tunable $π$-junction behavior and highlights the potential of BMS-based Josephson devices for phase-controllable superconducting electronics. Furthermore, in the presence of Rashba spin--orbit coupling, we find an anomalous Josephson effect characterized by a finite equilibrium supercurrent at zero phase difference. This behavior originates from the intrinsic breaking of time-reversal symmetry associated with the spin-polarized electronic structure of t...

items.title: OpenTherm: A Unified and Progressive Benchmark for 2.5D/3D-IC Thermal Prediction
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient chip thermal prediction is essential for advanced packaging design. In recent years, deep learning-based thermal predictors have made significant progress, achieving high prediction accuracy while substantially reducing computational costs. However, differences in datasets, simulators, and evaluation protocols hinder direct comparison of existing methods and systematic assessment of their generalization across design variations and cross-package transfer scenarios. We introduce OpenTherm, an open benchmark combining 32,000 established 3D-IC samples with 50,000 new 2.5D chiplet samples generated with the open-source HotSpot simulator. It provides fixed data splits, a common input representation, and shared evaluation tools. Five deployment-aligned Generalization Scopes cover fixed-design workload prediction, within-family layout, material, and cooling exploration, a...

items.title: Dual-Mode Exciton Coupling in Epitaxially Registered Organic-Inorganic 2D Heterocrystals
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA-MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic-inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. Monolayer-resolved PTCDA molecular crystals were grown on monolayer MoS2 via physical vapor assembly, and their crystallographic details, including the stacking angle, were determined by electron diffraction. Upon the formation of the heterostructures, PTCDA's photoluminescence was completely quenched because of organic-to-inorganic hole transfer, whereas that of MoS2 increased markedly with PTCDA thickness. items.title: First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions
items.abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that moderate strain can selectively enhance carrier transport without degrading optical transparenc...

items.title: Direct visualization of charge dynamics by Pockels imaging in optoelectronics
items.abstract: Understanding charge dynamics in optoelectronic devices is essential because it governs carrier transport, signal evolution, and device performance. Yet, experimental access to the spatiotemporal evolution of charge remains limited. Here, we introduce Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI), a sensitive, quantitative, and non-invasive pump-probe technique based on the linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect. CDPI images the electric-field wave associated with traveling photogenerated carriers and reveals the evolution of charge clouds in space and time. This provides direct access to fundamental transport processes, including drift, diffusion, carrier-carrier interactions, trapping, and detrapping. Furthermore, the internal conduction- and displacement-current profiles are obtained from the electric-field dynamics and shown to be consistent with the externally measured current transient...

items.title: 2D Transport in an in-plane magnetic field
items.abstract: A parallel in-plane magnetic field could, in principle, distinguish between two competing physical scenarios for the experimentally observed density-tuned 2D metal-insulator transition (where decreasing the carrier density leads to a crossover from an effective metal to an effective insulator): Wigner crystallization or Anderson localization. items.title: Overcoming configuration bottleneck: Modular pathways to stable semiconductor spin-qubit arrays
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor spin qubits have progressed from few-qubit demonstrations toward larger-scale devices fabricated in increasingly reproducible academic and industrial processes. This progress marks an inflection point: the central challenge is no longer to demonstrate high-fidelity operation in carefully tuned devices but to discover, verify, and maintain stable operating conditions reliably across many interdependent controls, varied device geometries, and disparate material platforms. In this Perspective, we frame spin-qubit operation as a modular automation problem. We decompose the workflow into five modules: bootstrapping from minimal prior information, configuration tuning, virtualization of physical gates into effective control axes, qubit-level tuning, and an operation layer with drift-aware maintenance.
